RESULT — Complete analysis executed (scripts/01_inventory.py, scripts/02_analysis.py; outputs in outputs/). Final data-grounded hypothesis:

**Hypothesis (answering the question).** In the NLSY79 snapshot provided, considering academic characteristics does NOT shrink the estimated race gap in college-track attainment — it reverses and amplifies it — while it DOES attenuate the family-SES associations. Rawly, Black (some-college rate 32.8% vs 39.6% for non-Black/non-Hispanic; logit b=-0.298, AME -0.068, p=0.034) and Hispanic (b=-0.210, AME -0.048, p=0.070) respondents aged ≥20 in 1979 were less likely to show college-track attainment (HGC1979≥13). Holding family-of-origin SES constant (parental education, 1979 family income, family size), the Black coefficient flips positive (M1: b=+0.622, AME +0.130); adding academic characteristics (ASVAB composite z; class standing in robustness) drives it further positive (M2: Black b=+1.218, AME +0.199; Hispanic b=+1.381, AME +0.219) because minorities are systematically lower on family SES and test scores (ASVAB means ≈442/421 vs 510) — a suppressor pattern: the apparent minority gap is explained (indeed over-explained) by SES plus test scores, leaving a conditional minority advantage. In contrast, the SES coefficients are attenuated by the academic block: mother's/father's education effects drop ~40% (0.574→0.345; 0.516→0.310) and a composite SES index drops ~70% (1.246→0.379) once ASVAB is added, i.e., a large share of the SES→attainment association runs through academic preparation. Moderation: race×SES (Black -1.294, Hisp -1.162, both p<0.001) and race×ASVAB (Black -0.432 p=0.052; Hisp -0.564 p=0.003) are negative, so SES and test-score gradients are flatter for Black/Hispanic respondents and the conditional advantage concentrates among lower-SES/lower-test-score minorities. The pattern (negative raw gap → positive conditional gap; ASVAB amplification) is robust across age cutoffs (≥19/20/21), median imputation, continuous-HGC OLS (Black -0.838→+0.158→+0.375), and an ever-college-housing outcome on the full sample.

**Limitation (one sentence).** BA receipt is not observable in this file — the only education variable is self-reported highest grade completed in 1979 (HGC≥16 yields only 24 analyzable cases) and ASVAB/class rank are measured in 1981 after that 1979 outcome — so all estimates describe college-track attainment (some college) by early adulthood and are an association-decomposition, not a temporal mediation or verified-BA analysis.

payload.hypothesis: In the NLSY79 snapshot, considering academic characteristics does NOT shrink the estimated race gap in college-track attainment — it reverses and amplifies it — while it DOES attenuate family-SES associations: raw Black/Hispanic disadvantages (~-7/-5 pp AME) flip to conditional advantages (~+20 pp) once SES and test scores are held constant (suppression), whereas parental-education effects drop ~40% and a composite SES index ~70% when ASVAB is added, and SES/test-score gradients are flatter for minorities (negative race x SES and race x ASVAB interactions).
payload.workflow: Nested logits M0(race+sex+age)->M1(+SES)->M2(+ASVAB; +class standing robustness) on HGC1979>=13 among age>=20 complete-case (n=2163), with age-cutoff, imputation, OLS-continuous-HGC, ever-college-housing, and HGC>=16-descriptive sensitivities; AMEs and % coefficient attenuation reported.
